featured_reviews.name: Kapil Bhatia
featured_reviews.review_text:
Positives:

Temperature-Controlled Pool – A big advantage, especially during rains and winter.
9-Foot Depth – Ideal for learning diving and improving treading water skills.
6-Day Availability – Open six days a week, making it easy to choose batches as per convenience.
Coaches – Highly professional, patient, courteous, dedicated, and knowledgeable.
All Swimming Strokes – Comprehensive training covering freestyle, breaststroke, backstroke, and butterfly.
Patient Learning Approach – Coaches ensure everyone learns at their own pace with proper attention.
Supportive Staff – Mouzam, Sakshi, and the entire administrative team are extremely helpful and cooperative.
All Age Groups Welcome – From kids as young as 5 to adults over 75, proving age is never a barrier.

My Journey:

I already knew breaststroke, but I always wanted to learn the other swimming styles. Like many, I never really found the time or push to start. When my wife joined the Michael Phelps Swimming program at Willingdon Sports Club, I would accompany her. One day, Mouzam encouraged me to join as well.

Initially, I was unsure—did I really need to learn new strokes? But I eventually decided to take the plunge, both literally and figuratively.

Starting out wasn’t easy. Learning new strokes felt challenging, but beginner coach Mahesh Sir played a key role in helping me pick up freestyle and backstroke. As I progressed, advanced coach Prayag Sir helped refine my breaststroke—I realized how much energy I had been wasting due to incorrect technique. He also guided me through learning butterfly, which is by far the most challenging stroke. Along the way, he fine-tuned all my strokes, especially backstroke and breaststroke.

Both coaches offered exceptional guidance, focusing on technique, form correction, drills, and personalized attention.

A special mention to Sameer Sir as well—though I had limited sessions with him, his professionalism and dedication stood out.

Even with prior knowledge of basic swimming, it took me nearly a year to confidently learn all strokes. The coaches and staff are incredibly friendly and always ready to help with any concerns.

A big thank you to Mahesh Sir, Prayag Sir, and Mouzam for their consistent support and dedication.

Final Thought:
The facility and coaching are excellent—but consistency is the key to truly learning and improving in swimming.

featured_reviews.name: Vijayshri
featured_reviews.review_text:
Khar Gymkhana, an iconic club founded in the late 1920s by a group of influential sports enthusiasts, has a rich history of nurturing talent and hosting prestigious tournaments. Over the decades, it has become a hub for a wide range of indoor and outdoor sports. The club offers excellent facilities for games like table tennis, billiards, cards, tennis, cricket, and swimming. In addition to the sports, Khar Gymkhana also boasts a popular restaurant called The Pavilion, known for its diverse menu of  food and drinks.

Membership to Khar Gymkhana is exclusive, with life membership available to individuals either within the immediate family or those married into a family that holds membership. There are also other types of memberships that can be obtained.

During our visit, we enjoyed a nice lunch and had time to observe some of the ongoing activities and games around the club. The food was delicious, and the service was surprisingly fast, considering the large crowd the restaurant was catering to. From the starters to the desserts, everything—whether vegetarian or non-vegetarian—was prepared well. However, there was one issue: the club lacked sufficient wheelchairs. A senior citizen in our group had to wait for a while to get access to one, as it was already in use by another member.

featured_reviews.name: anL
featured_reviews.review_text:
I rarely leave negative reviews, but after months of seeing the same problems and hearing the same complaints from other members, I feel this needs to be said.

The condition of this pool is simply unacceptable. Almost every time I visit, there are visible particles, bugs, slimy debris, and other contaminants floating in the water. The pool frequently looks dirty, and the filtration system rarely appears to be running. On one recent visit, the water was so dirty that I swam for barely two minutes before getting out and calling staff to inspect it. Instead of acknowledging the issue, I was told the pool was clean while visible debris remained in the water.

The area around the pool is no better. Rats, pigeons, and large insects are commonly seen around the facility, and there have been occasions where what appeared to be rat droppings were present near one of the staircases. For any swimming facility, this should be treated as a serious hygiene issue, not something that is repeatedly ignored.

The washrooms are honestly shocking. They often have a very strong smell, zero ventilation, and become unbearably hot. There is not even a fan in the bathroom area, making it feel like a sauna. The shower water pressure is so weak that it is barely usable. When concerns about the smell were raised, the response was essentially that it was “mostly the men’s washroom,” which completely misses the point. Members should not have to deal with that in the first place.

Maintenance across the facility appears to be severely neglected. Multiple tiles under the pool are cracked, the handrail used to enter the pool shakes and feels loose, and other damaged handrails seem to stay broken for months without repair. These are basic safety issues that should have been addressed long ago.

Another incident that I found highly unprofessional involved a female staff member sitting in the shower area wrapped only in a towel and appearing ready to use the same shower facilities as members. Regardless of the circumstances, this reflected poorly on the professionalism and management of the facility.

What is most frustrating is that these problems are not new. Virtually every regular member I have spoken to has complained about the same issues. The standard response is always “we’ll check” or “we’ll look into it,” yet nothing ever seems to change. Members are even told to come at different times if the pool is dirty, which is unreasonable. If the facility opens at 7:00 AM, the pool should be clean and ready to use at 7:00 AM—not hours later.

There is also often no visible attendant, maintenance staff member, or lifeguard around the pool area. For a facility charging members and operating a swimming pool, the lack of supervision is concerning.

At this point, the issue is not a dirty day or a one-off maintenance problem. It is a pattern of poor cleanliness, poor upkeep, and a management team that seems far more interested in dismissing complaints than fixing them. This facility has potential, but potential means very little when the same problems continue month after month despite repeated complaints from members.

There are far better-maintained pools in the area that take cleanliness, safety, and member concerns seriously. Based on my experience, I would not recommend this facility.

Decent place to hit the gym and then swim in the pool.

This place needs to be shut down and properly fixed and maintained before they ask people that pay their ridiculous rates for a very subpar experience.

featured_reviews.name: Rohit Venkat
featured_reviews.review_text:
I have to say, my visit to C'est La Vie on Hill Road, Bandra, through my Fitpass membership was nothing short of a nightmare. This place is an absolute disgrace. From the shady, dilapidated entrance to the gym’s basement location, everything screams neglect. The gym equipment is ancient, rusted, and downright dangerous. It feels like a health hazard rather than a place to work out. The dumbbells are corroded, many machines are out of order, and the whole place has a creepy, unkempt vibe.

The state of the bathrooms is appalling—they smell like a filthy public restroom and are in desperate need of cleaning and maintenance. The mirrors are stained, the floors are grimy, and the entire facility looks like it hasn’t seen a renovation since the early 2000s.

To make matters worse, the annual membership fee of 40,000 INR is a complete rip-off for such a shoddy, outdated facility. There are plenty of better, more modern gyms in the area at a fraction of the cost.

This place is a total scam and a health risk. Save your money and avoid this gym at all costs. I hope the management takes this feedback as constructive criticism and considers renovating the gym to improve the equipment and overall environment.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently completely refurbished and opened back to the general public.

Pool - 50 Metre Olympic spec. size with starting boards and lane markings (underwater).
Max depth- 17 Feet
Minimum Depth - 4 Feet
Lanes - 10
Access ladders - 6

The pool itself is very very good. The water is clean, minimal chlorine and no skin infections or rashes like you sometimes get with dirty water. The water filters seem to be working effectively.
Rules
Only swimers allowed onto the swim area level and around the pool.
Swimming costume is compulsory.

The facilities are well maintained, the staff are helpful and the overall experience is very good.

Timings
Morning 06.00am to 11.00am
Ladies 11.00am to 12.00pm

Evening 06.00pm to 10.00pm
Ladies 05.00 to 06.00pm

Overall Swimming Experience - 3/5

The Swimming experience itself is quite a mess. Filled with senior citizens/ middle-aged aged men with absolutely no sense of how a swimming pool works.
This is comparable to Mumbai traffic but in water.
People swim in any direction, breadth wise, diagonal wise, criss-crossing from anywhere and just getting into each other's way. There is absolutely no concept of swimming in a 50M pool and the crowd is comparable to a Waterpark on weekends.

If you're a casual swimmer just looking to get wet on a hot summers day then it's perfect.

If you're a professional swimmer looking to put in some practice laps when not coaching, then you will be disappointed.

It's impossible to actually swim 50M uninterrupted. Whatever the batch time.

The BMC should allocate a set timing slot morning/evening for serious swimmers only. Easier said than done though as its a common pool and arguments are bound to arise.

Overall the facilities are very good and the experience is nice but for competition level swimmers looking for extra practice it's not worth the time.

featured_reviews.name: Vasanth Pragash
featured_reviews.review_text:
November 2025 review

Pool is big and possibly olympic size. The pool has various depths starting from shallow end of 4 feet to over 15 feet depth. The pool is trifurcated into three areas, 1) Shallow end ,2) 2 Full length lanes( this reduces the width of the pool for the other 2) 3) Main pool area. Small lockers, shower rooms etc are available at no extra cost.

Membership process:
Full the details online in the website, be sure to upload aadhaar and pay the amount. For verification you will need aadhaar copy, printout of 2 receipts(one will become your id), original copy of doctors medical certificate stating you have no skin diseases or communicable diseases and are fit to swim, and three passport photos.They will take aadhaar copy, both receipt copies,the doctors medical certificate and photos. You will recive an SMS that registration is done and they will give you back one stamped receipt with your photo as your medical id. Laminate it or keep it in a ziplock bag.

Advantages:
1) Very friendly staff. They are extremely courteous and helpful in resolving pool queries and so on.
2) Very convenient timings. 6AM-12 noon (11-12 ladies only) and 5-10PM (5-6PM ladies only)
3) Pool is maintained very clean despite its public nature.

Disadvantages:
1) Nothing is provided, no soap, towels or paper.
2) You will need to bring your own locks, lockers are very small so make sure you buy a small lock.
3) Restrictions apply on swimwear , no full body suits for anyone and men can only wear swim shorts. No cotton shorts, etc allowed. If you come in morning you can buy swimming shorts, goggles and swim caps from the reception but it could be expensive.
4) Pool is extremely clorinated, and you can feel it in your teeth and hair. Be sure to brush and clean yourself as soon as your done with swimming. No shower doors for showers.
5) This is a public pool, which means a lot of people will be using it, this is understandable but can cause problems if your trying to swim laps as many kids/adults will crash your path. If this is the case stick to pool area 2).

Best time to swim would be 9-11 in the morning as a guy, most people are working and the sun is bright such that the pool isn't too cold.

featured_reviews.name: Aniket
featured_reviews.review_text:
Prabodhankar Thackeray Udyan in Vile Parle East is a small, green escape tucked beside the Prabodhankar Thackeray Swimming Pool. Built thoughtfully over what was once a dump yard, the transformation into a public garden has made it a popular spot for morning and evening walkers. The park sees a steady flow of senior citizens who enjoy the peaceful environment and leisurely strolls. Long benches line the pathways, allowing tired walkers a comfortable place to rest and enjoy the surroundings.

Inside the garden, there is a small Ganpati temple where people stop to pray, adding a spiritual touch to their daily routine. A modest playground area exists for kids, which is a great idea in concept, but unfortunately the maintenance leaves much to be desired. Several of the play structures are either broken or worn out, and the toilets, too, are not in the best condition.

On the positive side, the garden is rich in greenery and offers a refreshing environment. You’ll often come across many friendly cats that have made this space their home, adding a charming, albeit quirky, touch. Two-wheeler parking is convenient outside, while car parking can be quite challenging, especially in the mornings. Vendors selling fresh juices and soups outside the gate make it a pleasant stop after your walk.

featured_reviews.review_text:
One of Mumbai’s most well-planned and versatile sports complexes. It truly stands out as a one-stop gymkhana offering an impressive range of facilities under one roof.
The complex offers multiple sports options including Swimming, Rifle Shooting, Gymnastics, Table Tennis, Pickleball, Roller Skating and more, making it suitable for children, professionals, fitness enthusiasts and competitive athletes alike.
The infrastructure is modern, clean and well maintained, creating a great environment for training and recreation.
A big highlight is the Sollasa Sports Café, which serves quality food at reasonable prices—perfect for a healthy meal or quick snack after a workout or a game.
The Sports Recovery Centre is another major attraction, featuring Sauna, Steam, Massage and Hydrotherapy facilities, giving athletes and fitness lovers a professional space to recover and rejuvenate.
The Terrace Turf is ideal for a quick game of football and cricket, offering a great playing experience with a city view.
Complex also has at least two well-sized halls that are perfect for engagements, birthday parties, naming ceremonies, society meetings, and small get-togethers.
All in all, Prabodhan Thackeray Krida Sankul is a true one-stop destination for sports, fitness, recreation and social gatherings, offering excellent value for money and a wide variety of facilities rarely found together in Mumbai.

One of the highlights many visitors appreciate is the canteen. Known for its omelette and poha, it serves fresh, satisfying snacks and also offers a decent missal that regulars enjoy after their sessions.

The place is fairly well maintained and serves as a much-needed sports center for the residents of Vile Parle. With its growing range of facilities and community-friendly atmosphere, it continues to be an important recreational and fitness landmark in the locality.

featured_reviews.review_text:
This review is only for those parent(s) who are from middle class background and who know basic swimming that was learnt from their parents or from a professional and who are expecting that their child would pick basic swimming in their 60 sessions of Michael Phelps at Sahar Plaza Andheri East.

I would not recommend this place and instead if you have a pool within your society take your kid there and teach swimming as it is not rocket science but only practice. I enrolled my six year old daughter on 05/11/2025 with expiry on July 5, 2026 for 60 sessions as you can see from the swimming card. I was told that first 12 sessions was making the kid comfortable in water, gliding in water and jumping into water without fear which my daughter did. In reality, she was doing this for 15 sessions till I took them to task and asked them when they would start teaching her swimming that only then did they began her swimming classes. My kid was happy in the pool and was picking swimming quite well with confidence till 18th March on the 28th session when the head coach asked me about renewal as there was an offer going on. I told the coach that my expiry was not due and I will do it at that time irrespective of the offer. After that on the 29th session, the instructor who was teaching my kid started behaving oddly with my kid. He would instead of focussing on her swimming, started holding her when she was swimming or when she was jumping in water. Suddenly, in that one day, my daughter told me that if she didn’t swim properly, she would drown. The next session, I again noticed the same behaviour in the instructor and I realized that the instructor was hitting the confidence of my daughter by holding her hand when she jumped in the water which was never done with her. That was the last session of my daughter with Michael Phelps and on that day I gave earful to the head coach and questioned how the instructor had undermined the confidence of my kid. I told the head coach that till date the instructor never held the hand of my daughter whenever she jumped into the water and why did he hold only her hand and not the hand of any other kids who had jumped in the water. On hindsight, I realized that since I did not commit a renewal when asked to do so, the coaches decided to slow the progress of learning swimming of my kid so that I would do another 60 sessions and what is worse is for greed of money they hit the confidence of my kid in water by instilling fear of drowning so much so that it took me another 8 sessions in the pool of my society to rectify this fear. I decided to forgo the remaining 30 sessions of my daughter as I don’t want to entrust her with teachers who instilled fear instead of positive learning and it takes a long time to unlearn that instilled fear.
Coming to my background, I learnt swimming from my mother in a local pond in 10 days and so did my husband. After that, I sharpened my swimming with breathing technique in 15 days by a trainer. All my instructors be it my mother or the trainer told me only one thing – Be free in water and water will always push you upwards and the moment you struggle you will sink, so just be free in water and feel the water. This was a positive learning that I got about swimming. This learning takes time but it is positive learning and helps in swimming. The moment you talk to a child about drowning, the child learns fear not swimming.

So for those parents who think that their kid will learn swimming here in 60 sessions, its not going to happen without a renewal at Michael Phelps. The techniques taught here are all good but when a kid’s confidence is hit, it is difficult. If you have the money, then honey Michael Phelps is for you.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I am sharing this review to give honest feedback about this swimming centre.

The teachers and reception staff are generally helpful and sincere. One teacher noticed that my child was losing confidence and adjusted the training, which we really appreciated.

However, there are some areas where improvement is needed, especially since many young children attend these classes.

1. Cold Weather Conditions
Since this is an outdoor pool, strong winds blow directly onto the students during monsoon and winter. It feels cold even for parents sitting outside, and it is difficult for children after they come out of the water. When we raised this concern, we did not receive clear solutions.

2. Temperature-Regulated Pool
The pool is said to be temperature regulated, which is one reason we enrolled. However, during winter we were told that the heater was not working and would be started later. The water remained quite cold, making it difficult for children to complete their sessions comfortably.

3. Communication
Most staff members are polite, but one or two people sometimes speak in a way that feels a bit rude. A more friendly tone would help parents feel more comfortable.

4. Pool Support
There are no support rods or bars along the pool walls for children to hold. These would be helpful for beginners.

5. Washroom Facilities
Many mothers come with young children, but there is only one shower in the female washroom. Because of this, some people have to leave without washing after swimming.

Overall, the teachers are good, but some improvements in facilities and planning would make the experience much better for children and parents.
